next_step: Finalize region-by-region reserved GPU counts + sign NDA for security deep-dive
notes:
Account background:
- Global electronic marketplace for derivatives, strong bursty inference workload tied to market hours (NA + EU overlap).
- Already running some on-prem low-latency models, exploring Redwood Dedicated for consistent Q2 launch.

Conversation snapshot (shorthand / AE notes):
- 2026-01-18 discovery call (ff link above). AE: Maya. SE: Liam. Quote from head infra: "Need deterministic p95s during market open spikes — we can’t have variance."
- Primary ask: Reserved GPU pools across 3 regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with cross-region failover and 30% headroom for market spikes.
- Throughput target: sustained 400–600 concurrent requests to chat/rerank endpoints during open hours, bursts to 1.8k req/s for <60s.
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 25ms, p95 < 120ms for 256-token chat completion; p99 budgeted at 250ms only under rare failover scenarios.
- Model preference: prefer a quantized Llama-3-70B variant for balance of quality/cost; fallback to a 30B variant in constrained zones.

Dedicated capacity specifics being evaluated:
- Requested reserved GPU counts: initial ask = 24 A100-equivalent GPUs across regions (split 10 us-east / 8 eu-west / 6 us-west) + 30% failover headroom (planning number ~31 GPUs).
- Autoscaling policy: strict vertical autoscale discouraged; want pre-warm + predictable pool.
- Placement constraints: must be in customer VPC for eu-west and us-east; on-prem in a co-lo for a DR site in case of extended outage.
- Routing: primary-region affinity by customer, automatic cross-region fallback with cold-start mitigations (KV cache seeding).

POC & technical checkpoints:
- 2026-02-05 POC kickoff: ran synthetic traffic (weighting by real market traces) to validate kernel selection & batching behavior. Key findings: continuous batching reduced per-token cost but increased tail in naively configured queues.
- 2026-02-18 SE deep-dive: adjusted batching thresholds, KV cache TTL; p95 improved ~18% under test trace.
- 2026-03-02 SLA negotiation meeting: legal asked for clear credit model for failover-induced throttling; Ironridge requests a 15% service credit if regional failover increases p95 beyond 200ms for >10min.

Commercial & negotiation points:
- Ironridge prefers commit-based reserved pool (monthly billing) with firm throughput guarantees and a clear overage pricing band for burst capacity.
- Wants an explicit statement on failover headroom and how billing/commit reconciliation works if failover usage persists >72 hours.
- Request: Redwood to provide model performance profiles (latency/throughput per GPU type, with quantized options) per region to finalize GPU counts.

Open technical questions (short):
- How is KV cache replicated across regions for warm failover? Eager seed vs on-demand warming?
- Exact p99 attribution during multi-region failover (how do we measure and credit customers for transient infra events).
- Network egress/residency cost model for cross-region fallback.

Next steps (urgent):
- Deliver regionized sizing worksheet (Redwood SE) — due 2026-03-14.
- Sign NDA + schedule security deep-dive (legal + infra) week of 2026-03-21.
- Draft contract with dedicated commit tiers and explicit failover credit terms; procurement wants first draft in April.

Short notes / chatter style entries (as would appear in CRM):
- "If we can lock p95, procurement will move quickly" — Infra lead.
- SE concern: cache warming times during cross-region failover ~30–90s depending on sequence length, propose pre-seeded KV snapshots.
- Procurement: needs 30–60 day SLA review window; prefer monthly commitment to align with trading seasonality.

Attachments / references: sizing spreadsheet (drive), mock SLA clause (drive), ff recordings above.

Summary: High-value enterprise where reserved GPU pool topology + clear failover economics are deal drivers. Technical workstreams: sizing worksheet, cache-failover design, SLA credit formula. Commercial: commit-based monthly reserved pool with well-defined headroom and overage bands.

CRM tone: fragmented bullets, action-oriented, some quoted lines.
